verses.verse:
माला खण्डेन वाऽन्र्येन काष्ठोपकरणेन च।
पूरणीयौ ऋधौ तत्र लघु छिद्रं यथा भवेत्।56।
verses.text: Re and Dha should there be filled with a piece of a bead-string, or with some other wooden device, so that a small hole results.

commentary.text: This solution is possible in 3 ways. 1 Take one bead out of some mālā (string of beads) and seat it on the hole like a guṭakā (plug), so that the hole is closed like a phial [with its stopper]. Then the small hole of that plug should be enlarged only so far that the komal note is heard exactly right. But this procedure will not succeed in a six-hole bānsurī, because in it Re, on becoming komal, will spoil the Gāndhāra lying next to it. Although this difficulty occurs in the nine-hole flute too, in it a light chhallā (ring) is put into the separately made holes of komal Ga and Ni, and when Re and Dha are made komal those rings are removed. Or else bend a brass strip and put it inside the pipe, so that inside it fits to the very shape of the pipe, and by sliding it komal Gāndhāra can be brought back to how it was.
